idiom_name: validator table of function pointers applied before dispatch
implementation_notes: C has no request pipeline, so the classic structure is hand-written as an ordered table of function pointers - `static int (*const validators[])(const struct request *)` - run by one dispatcher before any handler is called; each validator returns 0 on acceptance and non-zero on rejection, and the table plus the reject path replaces the interceptor class hierarchy. Keep validators pure (no allocation, no I/O) and always route through the single dispatcher function; the manual form is justified whenever explicit, auditable control matters more than framework convenience, as in protocol or frame ingest.
pitfalls: A hand-written table rots: a validator added to one ingress path but not another silently drops coverage; keep exactly one dispatcher and make every path call it.
Return-code conventions are easy to invert (0 = ok versus 0 = error); pick one, document it, and treat unexpected or negative errno-style returns as rejection.
Validators that inspect strings must be bounded: strlen/strcpy on untrusted input is itself the vulnerability the layer is supposed to prevent.
